    <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">Building capability together – Dangerous Goods training

Dangerous Goods (DG) training is a vital part of keeping New Zealand’s aviation system safe.

Over the past two years, the Civil Aviation Authority has supported small aeroplane and helicopter operators by delivering DG training to help the sector transition to the updated competency based requirements under Civil Aviation Rule Part 92 and Advisory Circular AC92 1. This training was provided as an interim measure to assist sector capability and build operators’ confidence in meeting the new requirements.

The final CAA-delivered DG training course took place in February 2026.

As the regulator, our role is to set standards, provide guidance, and undertake oversight. Ongoing delivery of training is appropriately an industry function — and we’re confident the sector is well placed to lead in this space.

There is a real opportunity here for training providers to step forward and develop DG training that reflects the operational realities of small aeroplane and helicopter operators, including the remote environments many operate in.

If you’re interested in delivering this training, we’re keen to work with you. We can provide guidance on the regulatory requirements and certification pathway to help you get started.

Strong safety outcomes are achieved when we work together. We look forward to seeing industry capability continue to grow and strengthen.

From 1 July 2026, Medical Examiners will issue CAA medical certificates as PDFs via email, replacing laminated certificates sent by post. 

The change will make certificates faster and easier to access, store and present, either as a printed copy or on a device. Existing laminated certificates will remain valid until renewal. 

There are no changes to documentation requirements, the three components remain the same:
👉 Medical Certificate
👉 Medical Assessment Report
👉 Covering letter (if applicable)

This change reduces costs, is more convenient and simplifies the process for certificate holders.     <p class="attributed-text-segment-list__content text-color-text !text-sm whitespace-pre-wrap break-words
        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="main-feed-activity-card__commentary">It was great to host Acting Minister of Transport with responsibility for Aviation, Hon <a class="link" href="https://nz.linkedin.com/in/jamesmeagermp?trk=organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" target="_self" data-tracking-control-name="organization_guest_main-feed-card-text" data-tracking-will-navigate>James Meager MP</a>, at our CAA National Office yesterday to recognise the work of our Aviation Safety Oversight Group and the progress made over the past year to strengthen aviation safety and improve services for the sector. 🤝 📈 

The visit acknowledged the significant contribution they make to maintaining a safe aviation system while supporting innovation, growth and the day-to-day needs of aviation participants across New Zealand.

Over the past year the Aviation Safety Oversight has delivered improvements across certification and regulatory oversight, helping reduce delays and improve the experience of aviation participants interacting with the CAA. A key achievement has been completing CAA’s certification backlog through the “Get to Green” programme, improving timeliness and preventing future backlogs.

        " dir="ltr" data-test-id="feed-reshare-content__commentary">In 2022, we built our facility in Kerikeri, New Zealand with a clear goal: to be the first company to fly a traditionally crewed, fixed-wing aircraft autonomously in commercial revenue service in 2027.

We've made meaningful progress on our certification path in the first half of this year and believe we are entering the final phases before commercial service. Pending regulatory acceptance, we intend to launch commercial operations in New Zealand with certified aircraft flown by Merlin Pilot from takeoff to touchdown, under real regulatory oversight, on real routes, in revenue-generating operations.
